comments.note: SettingsViewModelTests.SaveCommand_RetriesThemeService_IfPreviousSetAsyncThrew: the bare `catch { /* expected on first call */ }` swallows all exception types, including unexpected ones such as NullReferenceException. If SaveCommand.ExecuteAsync ever throws a different exception (due to a different bug), the test would still reach its ThrowingThemeService.SetCallCount.Should().Be(1) assertion and likely mask the real problem. Consider narrowing to `catch (InvalidOperationException)` so that unexpected exception types propagate and fail the test visibly. Low risk given the tightly controlled stub, but precision here costs nothing and improves fault isolation.

FakeObfuscationService.LoadCallCount: property name tracks IsEnabledAsync call count. The name 'Load' is justified because SettingsViewModel calls ObfuscationVm.LoadAsync() which internally drives IsEnabledAsync — so 'Load' matches the ViewModel-level operation the test cares about. Nonetheless, a brief XML doc comment on the property could make the mapping explicit (e.g. 'Incremented each time IsEnabledAsync is called, which corresponds to ObfuscationSettingsViewModel.LoadAsync invocations'). No action required — flagged for awareness.

ThrowingThemeService.ThemeChanged event (inside SettingsViewModelTests) is never raised. This is correct interface compliance — no CS0067 warning because it is an interface implementation. The existing XML doc comment on the class adequately explains intent. No action required.
